changes.evidence: The initial is a tall undotted stem ending in a leftward bottom hook. Its height favours capital J, but it has no clear top bar and a lower-case j without a separately surviving dot remains possible. The crop does not settle case.

changes.location: heading, possible punctuation immediately after month
changes.evidence: A small dark downturned mark stands to the right of the final t stroke, separated by a pale interruption. It can be a point, but it can also be the broken terminal ductus of the t. The uncertain punctuation records the visible mark without declaring its intention.
The four year digits are physically below the month, aligned to the right; the place and day/month occupy the higher line. The original letter-heading line break is retained.
The short word shows a descending p, a low closed/flattened a and a short terminal r before the gap to les; no cancellation affects it. H's lexical doubt is removed.

The apparent lower stroke is the continuous returning descender of g, bending left under the beginning of the word. There is no separate horizontal rule beneath the remaining letters. No author emphasis is supplied.

changes.location: paragraph 2, cancelled letter between es and -tu
changes.h: es-tu; note says es replaces est
changes.evidence: The visible es is followed by a narrow upright with a lower loop/hook, crossed by several heavy short horizontal cancellation strokes. The underlying t is plausible but not wholly separable from those strokes. Deletion is certain; the identity of the letter remains doubtful. H already records the est correction in a note, so it is not treated as an omitted correction.

changes.location: paragraph 2, ending of serait/serais before physical line break
changes.evidence: After the dotted i the terminal rises in a tall hooked loop and returns to a heavy low knot. This can support t, but the heavy retracing does not exclude an elongated s. The addressed tu does not decide the glyph.

changes.location: paragraph 2, break between serait/serais and tu
changes.final: serait/serais tu, without a joining hyphen
changes.evidence: The crop shows blank space immediately to the right of the final letter at the end of its line. Half a shows the next line beginning directly with tu, without a preceding hyphen. Both sides of the physical break were inspected; only the ambiguous ending was cropped.

changes.location: paragraph 2, sign between position and Montpellier
changes.evidence: There are two separate filled marks, one small upper dot and one heavier lower lozenge, vertically aligned. No baseline a-loop or grave-accent stroke survives. This resolves the C doubt in favour of a colon; syntax is not used to change it.
The word begins with the tall crossed f, then low a-v-o-r strokes, a detached i dot and a terminal s. There is no t ascender or the additional internal letter sequence required for fantaisies.
A low n and a lead into the descending, left-returning loop of g, followed by e and a short r. The strokes support nager directly, so H's doubt is removed.
The long lower curve joins the descending g and sweeps back left; no independent underline continues beneath the full word. It is a letter descender, not a separately drawn emphasis rule.

The mark over i is one compact dot, without two roof arms: no circumflex is supplied. The first-vowel mark is a long almost vertical stroke, slightly leaning down to the right in the crop. That favours a grave direction but leaves an acute direction plausible in this hand; the retained doubt is now about the first accent, not an inferred circumflex.

changes.location: paragraph 3, cancelled material after constructive pour
changes.evidence: Repeated oblique cancellations run through low loops and a surviving tall medial stem. The group has an internal gap, but the writing elsewhere also separates letters widely, so even a two-word division is not secure. Attempts to recover a full word fail at the opening and middle; one unreadable word is retained as the estimate.

changes.location: paragraph 3, adjective between une and approche
changes.evidence: The crop shows p-r-e-m-i, the accented short e stroke, and a final arching r ending downwards. A clear blank follows before approche; there is no terminal e loop or additional stroke. The written ending premièr is retained.

Under the cancellation, an initial angled rise, low rounded form and short crossed upright can be read as nat-, while a taller loop later and the surviving low final -ment also leave évidemment possible. The middle is overwritten too heavily for a unique reading. Naturellement is the slightly better stroke-led attempt; neither candidate is asserted as certain. The cancellation state is clear.

changes.location: paragraph 3, comma after cancelled adverb / inserted bien sûr
changes.evidence: A separate short oblique comma remains at baseline to the right of the cancelled group and before le. It is outside the heavy deletion strokes; the above-line replacement occupies that adverb position, leaving the comma live.

The lower horizontal remnants are preceded by a short low detached tail that favours q; a small mark to their upper right can be an apostrophe. The q body is washed out and nearby flecks complicate the detached marks, so où au remains a possible alternative. The context is not substituted for the lost strokes.
One continuous oblique slash rises between the crossed 7 and the following 1; no second separating stroke or dash is present.
The compact pro is followed by a tall descending f, with a separate point to its lower right. The abbreviation is not expanded in the page text.
A low n-shaped stroke is followed by a distinct short horizontal dash, then catégorie. It is not an infinity loop or a numeral.
The first sign is one upright numeral 1 with a short foot; a separate hyphen precedes cat. A point after t and the following et are both visible. The sheet ends there.

coverage: Completed one layout view of the whole 1688 × 2372 image, then one sequential view of each supplied half, reading every physical body line and every agreed word and sign against both full witness texts. The date, salutation, all three paragraphs, both page-number systems, all three deletions and both above-line insertions are inventoried. The source has no display, diagram, drawing or separate marginal prose note. Heading line breaks are preserved; body line wraps and line-end word divisions are joined. The alleged inversion hyphen was checked on both sides of its line break. Nine still-unresolved loci received exactly one tight crop each.
